plan.target: Spurious Illegal Instruction Exception on satp Access When Virtual Memory is Disabled (src/privileged/csrs.sv)
plan.rationale: In `src/privileged/csrs.sv`, `satp` (CSR 0x180) handling contains an erroneous gating check in its read decoder. At lines 91-94, the hardware correctly implements the architectural rule that `satp` is hardwired to 0 (Bare mode) when virtual memory is not implemented: `if (P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED) flopenr #(P.XLEN) SATPreg(...) else assign SATP_REGW = '0;`. However, in the read decode multiplexer at lines 158-159, `csrs.sv` gates the access with `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED`: `SATP: if (P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & (PrivilegeModeW == P.M_MODE | ~STATUS_TVM)) CSRSReadValM = SATP_REGW; else IllegalCSRSAccessM = 1'b1;`. When `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED == 0` (present in all configurations supporting Supervisor mode without an MMU, such as `nodcache_rv64gc`, `noicache_rv64gc`, `nocache_rv64gc`, `nodcache_rv32gc`), line 159 asserts `IllegalCSRSAccessM = 1'b1`. This causes `src/privileged/csr.sv` to assert `IllegalCSRAccessM`, triggering a spurious Illegal Instruction exception (Cause 2) on any attempt to read or write `satp` in M-mode or in S-mode with TVM=0. According to the RISC-V Privileged Architecture Specification (v20211203, Section 4.1.11), `satp` is a mandatory Supervisor register whenever S-mode is implemented; when address translation is not supported (only Bare mode is supported), `satp` must be read-only zero (hardwired to 0) and must not raise an illegal instruction exception for privileged accesses. The Spike oracle correctly allows access to `satp` without trapping, while Wally erroneously traps.
plan.tester_prompt:
Investigate and construct a deterministic reproducer for the spurious Illegal Instruction exception on `satp` (CSR 0x180) access when virtual memory is disabled (`P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED == 0`).

### 1. Target Hardware & Logic
- RTL Source Files:
  - `src/privileged/csrs.sv`:
    - Lines 91-94: `if (P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED) flopenr #(P.XLEN) SATPreg(...); else assign SATP_REGW = '0; // hardwire to zero if virtual memory not supported`. Line 94 correctly hardwires `SATP_REGW` to 0.
    - Lines 158-159: `SATP: if (P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & (PrivilegeModeW == P.M_MODE | ~STATUS_TVM)) CSRSReadValM = SATP_REGW; else IllegalCSRSAccessM = 1'b1;`. The inclusion of `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED &` in the `if` condition erroneously causes `IllegalCSRSAccessM = 1'b1` to be asserted whenever `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED == 0`, overriding `SATP_REGW` and converting valid accesses into illegal instruction exceptions.
    - Lines 77-83: `assign WriteSATPM = CSRSWriteM & (CSRAdrM == SATP) & (PrivilegeModeW == P.M_MODE | ~STATUS_TVM) & LegalSatpModeM & P.SV39_SUPPORTED;`. Write logic correctly suppresses register updates when virtual memory is unsupported.
  - `src/privileged/csr.sv`:
    - Line 317: `assign IllegalCSRAccessM = ((IllegalCSRCAccessM & IllegalCSRMAccessM & IllegalCSRSAccessM & IllegalCSRUAccessM | InsufficientCSRPrivilegeM) & CSRReadM) | IllegalCSRMWriteReadonlyM;`. When `IllegalCSRSAccessM` is 1, `IllegalCSRAccessM` is asserted, taking an illegal instruction trap (Cause 2).
- Target Configuration:
  - Use configuration `WALLYCONF=nodcache_rv64gc` (located at `config/deriv/nodcache_rv64gc/config.vh`), where `S_SUPPORTED = 1`, `U_SUPPORTED = 1`, `ZICSR_SUPPORTED = 1`, and `SV39_SUPPORTED = 0` / `SV32_SUPPORTED = 0` (so `VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED = 0`).
  - Alternative configuration: `nocache_rv64gc` or `noicache_rv64gc`.

### 2. Normative Specification Requirements
- RISC-V Instruction Set Manual, Volume II: Privileged Architecture (v20211203):
  - Section 4.1.11 ('Supervisor Address Translation and Protection (satp) Register'): 'The satp register is an S-mode WARL register... When satp.MODE is Bare, supervisor virtual addresses are equal to supervisor physical addresses, and there is no additional memory protection beyond the physical memory protection scheme... When address translation is not supported (only Bare mode is supported), satp is read-only zero (hardwired to 0).' Non-existence of `satp` is only permitted when Supervisor mode is not implemented at all.
  - Section 3.1.6.5 ('Trap Virtual Memory (TVM) in mstatus'): 'When TVM=1, attempts to read or write the satp CSR or execute an SFENCE.VMA or SINVAL.VMA instruction while executing in S-mode raise an illegal instruction exception. When TVM=0, these operations are permitted in S-mode.' M-mode access is never restricted by TVM.
  - Section 2.1 ('CSR Addresses'): Accessing an existing CSR with sufficient privilege must not cause an illegal instruction exception.

### 3. Hypothesized Failure
- Under `nodcache_rv64gc` (`P.S_SUPPORTED == 1` and `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED == 0`):
  - In M-mode, executing `csrr t1, satp` or `csrw satp, t1` incorrectly triggers an Illegal Instruction exception (Cause 2) on Wally because line 159 asserts `IllegalCSRSAccessM = 1'b1`.
  - In S-mode with `mstatus.TVM == 0`, executing `csrr t1, satp` incorrectly triggers an Illegal Instruction exception (Cause 2).
- Under Spike (`spike --isa=rv64gc`):
  - `csrr t1, satp` executes legally in M-mode and S-mode (when TVM=0), returning 0 without trapping.

### 4. Directed Test Suite
Construct standalone assembly tests using the harness pattern established in the workspace (see `tests/test.ld` and `runs/20260913T023615Z-f48825c5/tests/test.S`):
- **Test A (Bug Trigger 1 - M-mode CSR Read)**: Execute `csrr t1, satp` (0x180) in M-mode.
  - Trap handler checks if trap occurred: if trap occurs, fail (`a0 = 1; j exit`).
  - Verify `t1 == 0`.
- **Test B (Bug Trigger 2 - M-mode CSR Write)**: Execute `csrw satp, t1` (with value 0 or non-zero WARL test) in M-mode.
  - Trap handler checks if trap occurred: if trap occurs, fail (`a0 = 2; j exit`).
- **Test C (Bug Trigger 3 - S-mode CSR Read with TVM=0)**: Transition to S-mode with `mstatus.TVM = 0` (and configure PMP so S-mode can execute code: e.g., set `pmpaddr0 = -1`, `pmpcfg0 = 0x1F`). Execute `csrr t1, satp`.
  - Trap handler checks if trap occurred: if trap occurs, fail (`a0 = 3; j exit`).
- **Test D (Positive Control 1 - S-mode CSR Read with TVM=1)**: In S-mode with `mstatus.TVM = 1`, execute `csrr t1, satp`.
  - Expected: Trap with Cause 2 on both Wally and Spike (mandated by TVM).
- **Test E (Positive Control 2 - U-mode Access Trap)**: In U-mode, execute `csrr t1, satp`.
  - Expected: Trap with Cause 2 on both Wally and Spike (mandated by CSR privilege level).

### 5. Execution, Oracle & Reproducer Rules
- Independent Oracle: Run compiled ELF with `/opt/riscv/bin/spike --isa=rv64gc <elf>`. Spike must exit 0 on all tests.
- Wally DUT: Rebuild using `make -C sim/verilator compile WALLYCONF=nodcache_rv64gc TESTBENCH=testbench`.
- Run Wally via `./sim/verilator/wkdir/nodcache_rv64gc_testbench/Vtestbench +ElfFile=<path_to_elf>`.
- When a test failure occurs on Wally, trigger an unhandled trap (`csrw mtvec, x0; jr x0`) to cleanly trigger the testbench assertion failure (`Assertion failed in testbench: Program fetched illegal instruction 0x00000000... Verilog $stop`), giving exit code 134 on mismatch.
- When tests pass, write 1 to `tohost` (`sd a0, 0(t0)`) and execute `j .` (`0x0000006f`) to signal test completion, exiting cleanly with code 0.
- Strictly follow `loop.py` directory rules: create test sources once under `$test_dir/tests/` before invoking `reproducer.sh`. All build artifacts, ELFs, dumps, and logs MUST be placed in `$test_dir/build/` and `$test_dir/logs/`. Never write or modify files outside `build/` and `logs/` during `reproducer.sh`.
- Exit codes for `reproducer.sh`: exit 0 if Wally DUT passes (no bug), exit 1 ONLY if Wally exhibits the functional mismatch (reproducer reproduces bug), exit 2 for build/tool/environment errors.

fixer.report:
Root Cause: In src/privileged/csrs.sv line 158, the SATP CSR read decode condition `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & (PrivilegeModeW == P.M_MODE | ~STATUS_TVM)` erroneously includes a `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED &` guard. When `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED == 0` (as in `nodcache_rv64gc`), this condition always evaluates to 0 regardless of privilege mode, falling through to `IllegalCSRSAccessM = 1'b1` on line 159. This causes a spurious Illegal Instruction exception (Cause 2) on any attempt to read or write the `satp` CSR, even in M-mode. Per RISC-V Privileged Architecture v20211203 Section 4.1.11, when address translation is not supported, `satp` must be hardwired to 0 (correctly implemented at line 114) but must remain accessible without trapping for privileged accesses.

Minimal Fix: Removed `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED &` from the condition on line 158 of src/privileged/csrs.sv. The corrected line reads: `SATP: if (PrivilegeModeW == P.M_MODE | ~STATUS_TVM) CSRSReadValM = SATP_REGW;`. The privilege-only check is correct because the register value is already hardwired to 0 when VIRTMEM is unsupported, and the write path already correctly suppresses updates via `& P.SV39_SUPPORTED`.

Files Changed: src/privileged/csrs.sv (line 158, single guard removal).

Targeted-Test Outcome: Reproducer script executed successfully. The Wally DUT now passes all 5 test cases (M-mode read, M-mode write, S-mode read with TVM=0, S-mode trap with TVM=1, U-mode trap) in `nodcache_rv64gc` configuration, exiting with code 0. Spike oracle also passes with exit code 0. Build succeeded with no errors.
